relations: Vero 与 Kayla 是恋人：Kayla 说 “I love you, Vero, and I know you love me”、“call you mine”，并提醒 “please remember you chose me, too”；Vero 答 “I love you just as much as I love him”
Vero 与 Brawley 是恋人：“that normally only happens after Brawley fucks the thoughts out of me”，Kayla 也说 “Fuck, I love him and you.”
Aaron 是 Kayla 的旧伴侣兼施暴者，“before I knew what kind of monster Aaron was”，伤她左髋并留下疤痕 “a scar on your left hip”
Vero 与 Aaron 敌对：“I stabbed him with a screwdriver”、“if he wasn’t dead, I would hunt him down and kill him again”
Vero 是 Banks 的委托方：Banks 制作 Kayla 的等身蜡像并称 “My best piece to date”，Vero 直接签字；Ares 与 Kayla 是工作关系（“before Ares comes to find her for work”）；Clay 与 Kayla 是恋人（“the woman I’m fucking”）
numbers: from the first moment I said it

facts.fact: Kayla 以口交方式叫醒 Vero，并说是 Brawley 出的主意要她{EM}有创意地叫醒他
facts.anchor: Brawley told me to be creative waking you up.

facts.fact: Vero 在床上开口坦承：在棚屋里 Aaron 提到 Kayla 左髋的疤痕，Vero 听出他在挑拨后用螺丝刀捅了 Aaron
facts.anchor: In the shed when I was with Aaron, he said something about a scar on your left hip.

facts.fact: Kayla 说出当年真相：她还不知道 Aaron 是什么样的人时两人在厨房争吵，Aaron 说那是意外、她才是动刀的人，她因为爱他而信了，还帮他处理伤口
facts.anchor: He said it was an accident, that I turned into the knife.

facts.fact: Kayla 承认 Aaron 把疤称作惩罚并以此为傲；Vero 吻去她眼泪并说 {L}Paper-cut princess, don{AP}t cry{R}
facts.anchor: “He told me it was a punishment. That he was proud of it.”

facts.fact: Kayla 告诉 Vero 他无法阻止任何一件事、包括刚刚发生的事；Vero 回应说自己宁可死也绝不在她身上留下任何痕迹
facts.anchor: But just know I would die before I ever put a mark on you.

facts.fact: Kayla 让 Vero 明白她现在有他们、可以成为任何版本的自己，并承诺做最好的自己、永远站在他这边；Vero 静默流泪
facts.anchor: You have us now, and can be any version of yourself that you want to be.

facts.fact: Vero 趁 Kayla 洗澡时溜去找 Banks，用没读的 paperwork 签字，把盖着布的等身蜡像装上手推车推回住宅区
facts.anchor: Banks loads her onto a trolley, and I wheel her out, fully covered, carefully wheeling her back to the residential area.

facts.fact: Vero 在厨房当众掀开蜡像上的布；Clay 拒绝把它放在冰箱旁，Kayla 提议放进 Clay 在 Asylum 的房间并要求{EM}今天先留下
facts.anchor: “Absolutely not,” Clay scoffs. “I am not eating breakfast opposite that every morning, Vero. It will stare at me . . . it has her eyes.”
